one_line: A Western Ganga courtier and riverine administrator at the Talakad capital on the Kaveri in the 5th–6th century CE.

appearance.age_look: Early thirties, lean but athletic build, upright posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with medium-brown Kaveri-basin complexion, straight nose, sharp jawline, neatly trimmed moustache, expressive dark eyes with a calm but alert default expression.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair parted slightly off-center, drawn back into a small, tidy topknot at the back of the crown; simple narrow gold band circling the head, and a soft white turban-cloth wrapped low around the knot like a headscarf, leaving forehead and ears visible.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate mid-5th–6th century Western Ganga noble attire: an off-white, finely woven cotton uttariya (upper cloth) draped over both shoulders and crossing diagonally over the chest, secured with a plain gold clasp near the right collarbone; beneath it, a fitted pale-sandalwood-coloured long-sleeve tunic reaching just past the hips, with a modest round neckline and subtle woven border in dark green; lower garment is a dark green cotton dhoti-style drape tightly wrapped from waist to ankles with clean pleats in front, bordered at hem with a simple gold stripe; leather sandals appropriate to the period; jewellery limited to a short, thick gold neck-torque, two modest gold bangles on each wrist, and small round gold ear-studs, all kept understated to emphasize practicality; a folded palm-leaf bundle tucked at his waist on the left side to suggest record-keeping; overall textiles appear matte and handwoven, with minimal patterns beyond simple borders.
appearance.signature: A long wooden staff of office about his own height, dark-brown polished hardwood with a subtly carved lotus-bud finial at the top and a narrow bronze band near the upper grip, carried upright in his right hand as a symbol of authority in river and land administration.

ref_desc: Dharmapala of Talakad has an oval medium-brown face with a moustache, black hair in a small topknot wrapped with a white headcloth and gold band, wearing an off-white uttariya over a pale-sandalwood tunic and dark green dhoti, gold jewellery, and carrying a dark-brown lotus-tipped staff.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Dharmapala of Talakad: an early-thirties Western Ganga courtier with an oval medium-brown face, sharp jawline, straight nose and calm, alert dark eyes, sporting a neatly trimmed moustache. His thick black hair is parted slightly off-center, pulled back into a small topknot at the back of the crown, wrapped with a soft white headcloth low around the knot, and encircled by a narrow gold band, leaving his forehead and ears visible. He wears an off-white cotton uttariya draped over both shoulders and crossing diagonally over the chest, fastened near the right collarbone with a plain gold clasp, over a fitted pale-sandalwood long-sleeve tunic that reaches just past the hips and has a simple round neckline and a subtle dark green woven border. His lower garment is a dark green cotton dhoti-style drape wrapped from waist to ankles with clean front pleats and a single gold stripe at the hem, paired with simple leather sandals. Jewellery is modest: a short thick gold neck-torque, two plain gold bangles on each wrist, and small round gold ear-studs; a folded palm-leaf bundle sits tucked at his left waist. In his right hand he carries his signature long wooden staff of office, as tall as he is, made of polished dark-brown hardwood with a carved lotus-bud finial on top and a narrow bronze band near the upper grip. Use a palette of off-white, dark green, pale sandalwood, gold, and dark brown, and present him front-facing with clear views of face, hair, garments, jewellery, and staff for consistent redrawing.
